name: Cappuccino
caffeine: From the espresso alone, usually a double; the milk and foam add none.

house.ask: Not printed on our menus: ask at lineup whether there is an espresso machine, whether the bar will make a cappuccino, and at what price.

what: Espresso under milk stretched longer, so it wears a real cap of foam, a third to a half inch deep, in a 5 to 6 oz cup. Equal thirds of espresso, milk and foam is a teaching phrase, not a measure. Against a flat white of the same size, the difference is air.
taste: Sweet and airy, the coffee cutting through the middle; lighter than a flat white because of the air.

steps: Pull a double, 18 to 20 g in, 36 to 40 g out, into a warmed cup.
Start with 3 to 3.5 oz cold milk, less than for a flat white, since it gains volume.
Stretch longer, a steady tearing hiss, then sink the tip and spin until glossy.
Cut the steam near 135 to 140F (57 to 60C), swirl, and pour so the foam domes to the rim.
make.ratio: Italian single spec: 0.8 oz espresso to 3.4 oz cold milk
make.dose: 18 to 20 g coffee; 3 to 3.5 oz milk
make.time: Shot 25 to 30 seconds; serve at once
make.cup: Warmed 5 to 6 oz cup on a saucer

serve: In a warmed cup on a saucer with a teaspoon, the handle towards the guest's right hand. Out fast, because the cap dries the moment the drink stops moving; cocoa only if the bar does it.
story: The name comes from the Capuchin friars, whose brown habits matched coffee lightened with milk. Vienna's coffee houses called a coffee with cream a Kapuziner, possibly in the eighteenth century, and the Italian name followed later. In Italy it is a morning drink, which travelled guests like to mention.
guest: Espresso with steamed milk and a deeper cap of foam: lighter and airier than a latte, in a smaller cup.
watch: Big dry bubbles and foam separating from the milk are the fault, not a thick cap.
A dry cappuccino means more foam, less milk: the older stiff style, which holds no pattern.
Never re-steam leftover milk: the foam will not come back and it tastes cooked.

study: The heart is floated, not drawn

recall.answer: A double espresso in a warmed 5 to 6 oz cup, under about 3 oz of milk stretched longer into a third to a half inch of glossy foam. Sweet and airy, the coffee through the middle.

quiz.q: Against a flat white of the same size, what mainly sets a cappuccino apart?
quiz.explain: Less milk and a longer stretch: the difference is air. Milk at 170F (77C) is cooked.

quiz.q: The name is usually traced to what?
quiz.explain: Coffee lightened with milk matched the friars' brown habits; Vienna's Kapuziner came before the Italian name.

quiz.q: A guest orders a dry cappuccino. What do they want?
quiz.explain: Dry means more foam and less milk, the older stiff style. It is a request, not a fault.
